transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what finally pushed me to make the appointment is... my eating has just been completely all over the place. Like, some weeks I barely even touch my dinner. I'll make a whole meal, like a pot roast. I used to make this really good pot roast back when I was taking some classes at the community college—my roommate just loved it, with the little carrots and potatoes, the whole thing. But lately, I just look at dinner and can't eat it. 

And then, I don't know, other nights I'll just stand in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone’s gone to bed. The kitchen gets so drafty at night, actually. I keep meaning to call the landlord about the window above the sink, the weather stripping is completely gone, but he never really fixes anything anyway. Last year it took him three weeks to fix a leaky faucet. So I'm just standing there freezing in the dark, eating sleeves of crackers... but yeah, my appetite is just everywhere right now.
When you find yourself eating in that way, are you doing it because you are specifically worried about your body shape or your weight?

No, no, it's not about my weight or anything like that. I don't really think about my shape much these days. Actually, I used to worry about it more when I was younger, back when I worked at this little boutique downtown. We had to wear these really fitted clothes, and the lighting in the dressing rooms was just awful. It made everyone look sort of... green? Like a sickly green. My manager, Brenda, she was always complaining about the lights, but she never did anything about it. She was more worried about organizing the scarf display by color. We had hundreds of scarves. Silk ones, wool ones... I had this one beautiful blue silk scarf that I wore all the time, but I lost it on the bus one day. The number 14 bus, I think. It's always so crowded on the 14, especially around 5 o'clock. But anyway, no, I'm not eating like that because of my weight.
How long have you been feeling this way, where your appetite and mood have been so inconsistent?

Well, let's see... it's been a while now. I'd say about two years and five months? Yeah, that sounds right. It all started right around the time the arguments at home got really bad. We were fighting so much about my spending, and my art projects. I had this vision for a giant papier-mâché sculpture in the living room, a sort of abstract tree, you know? I bought all this chicken wire and flour and old newspapers. The Sunday paper is the best for papier-mâché because the sheets are so big, especially the arts and leisure section. I used to love reading the arts and leisure section on Sunday mornings with a cup of coffee. I had this favorite mug, it was yellow with little blue daisies on it, but the handle broke off in the dishwasher. Dishwashers are so rough on ceramics, don't you think? I tried to glue it back on with that super glue, the kind that comes in the tiny little tubes, but it just got all over my fingers. My fingers were stuck together for hours! I had to use nail polish remover to get it off, and it smelled awful. But anyway, yeah, the arguments about the art supplies and the money really escalated about two years and five months ago, and that's when everything just sort of went haywire.
During these past two years and five months, have there been any periods of two months or longer where you felt mostly like your usual self and did not experience these mood or appetite struggles?

Two months? Um... no, I don't think so. It's just been a constant rollercoaster, honestly. I haven't really felt like my usual self since... well, since before the papier-mâché tree. I really wish I could have finished that tree. It was going to have these beautiful, sweeping branches that reached all the way to the ceiling. The ceiling in our living room has that popcorn texture, you know? I've always hated popcorn ceilings. They just gather dust, and they're impossible to clean. My cousin Shirley tried to scrape the popcorn texture off her ceiling once, just with a putty knife and a spray bottle of water. She made such a mess. There was wet, gloppy plaster all over her carpet, and it dried into these hard little clumps. She had to rent a steam cleaner from the grocery store to get it out. Those steam cleaners are so heavy to lug into the car. I remember helping her lift it into the trunk of her Honda Civic. The trunk was already full of old gardening tools, because she was really into growing her own tomatoes that summer. Beefsteak tomatoes, I think. They were huge, but they tasted a little watery. But no, I haven't had a break for two months. It's just been going and going.
During these past two years, have you felt down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I do. I go through these stretches where the whole house just feels... gray, you know? Heavy. I'll just sit at the kitchen table feeling totally empty, even if nothing terrible has actually happened that day. I just sit there staring out the window. The window looks out over the neighbor's yard, the Hendersons. They have this massive oak tree that drops leaves all over our driveway. Mr. Henderson is always out there with his leaf blower, usually right when I'm trying to watch my morning shows. It's one of those gas-powered ones, so loud. I don't know why he doesn't just use a rake. Raking is supposed to be good exercise, right? My aunt used to say it was good for your core. She was really into Pilates before it was popular. She had this VHS tape of Pilates routines that she played every single morning. The tracking on the tape was terrible, so the picture was always jumping up and down, but she didn't care. She just kept doing those leg lifts. But yeah, I do get those heavy, empty feelings a lot.

During these past two years, have you ever experienced periods lasting at least a few days where you felt unusually energetic, restless, or irritable, needing much less sleep than usual, or having your thoughts racing?

Oh, definitely. I get these bursts where I just feel so bright and totally unstoppable, like I can do absolutely anything. I won't sleep for days, and my mind is just flying. But then, out of nowhere, I get so furious. Just incredibly irritable over the smallest things. Like the other day, my husband moved my paints. He just shifted them to the other side of the desk, but it made me so angry! Or if he questions a receipt I bring home. He's always asking about receipts. He keeps them all in this old shoebox in the closet. It's a New Balance shoebox, the blue and white kind. He loves those sneakers. He says they're the only ones with good arch support. He has flat feet, you see. He went to a podiatrist a few years ago who told him he needed custom orthotics, but they were so expensive, so he just buys the New Balance ones. He wears them everywhere, even when he's mowing the lawn. The grass stains get all over the white mesh, and they look terrible. I tried scrubbing them with baking soda and an old toothbrush once. Toothbrushes are really good for cleaning grout, too. I use a red one for the bathroom tiles. But anyway, yeah, I get so mad at him when he asks about the receipts when I'm feeling that way.

During those times when you felt unstoppable and had racing thoughts, have you ever had a period where that went on for at least an entire week, or where it became so intense that you required hospitalization?

Um, a whole week? No, I don't think they last that long. It's usually just a few days of feeling like I'm on top of the world before I crash or get so mad. And I've never had to go to the hospital for it. I really hate hospitals anyway. The lighting is always so terrible, those long fluorescent tubes that hum all the time. It gives me a headache just thinking about it. My sister had to stay in the hospital for a week when she had her gallbladder out. She complained about the food every single day. She said the Jell-O was always warm and the broth tasted like dishwater. She ended up sneaking in a bag of those little powdered donuts, the ones with the white sugar all over them. She got powdered sugar all over her hospital gown. It was hilarious, but the nurses were not amused. They had to change her bedding and everything. Hospital sheets are always so stiff, aren't they? They must use a ton of bleach. Bleach is so bad for the environment, you know. I try to use vinegar and baking soda for most of my cleaning now. It smells like a salad dressing for a little while, but it works just as well. But no, I haven't been hospitalized for feeling energetic, and it doesn't last a whole week.

During these past two years, have there been times when your 'heavy' or 'gray' feelings were so severe that you could not function at work or at home, or felt completely unable to experience any pleasure in things you usually enjoy for two weeks or more?

Yeah, definitely. There are these long stretches, definitely more than two weeks, where I just can't bring myself to do anything I normally love. Things I used to look forward to, like my book club, or cooking, going to art galleries, even just tending to my rose beds... they all just feel like these massive chores that I keep putting off. The roses especially. I have these beautiful David Austin roses, the 'Gertrude Jekyll' variety. They're supposed to have this incredible, strong old rose scent, but you have to prune them just right or they get all leggy. I bought these special pruning shears from a catalog last spring. The catalog was from this company in England, and everything in it looked so perfectly manicured. They had these gorgeous copper watering cans, too. I almost bought one, but my husband said it was ridiculous to spend that much on a watering can when the plastic one from the hardware store works just fine. He's always so practical like that. Sometimes I wish he'd just let me have something pretty just for the sake of it, you know? But anyway, yeah, when I get in those gray moods, I don't even care about the roses or the book club or anything. It's just too much effort.
During these past two years and five months, have these periods of feeling 'up' and feeling 'down' occurred for at least half of the time?

Yeah, I'd say so. Looking back, those periods where I'm just so... expansive, you know, overcommitted and doing everything, they've actually taken up more of the past couple of years than the depressed stretches or the calmer gaps in between. It's like I'm always on the go. Which reminds me, I signed up to organize the neighborhood block party this year. It's a huge undertaking, really. We're going to have a bouncy house for the kids and a potluck. I've been trying to find a good recipe for a pasta salad that doesn't use mayonnaise, because mayo goes bad so quickly in the sun. My aunt Clara used to make this amazing macaroni salad with celery and little cubes of cheddar cheese, but she always used Miracle Whip. I don't really like the sweetness of Miracle Whip. It tastes too artificial to me. I prefer real mayonnaise if I'm going to use it, like Hellmann's. Or Best Foods, I think they call it out West. It's funny how the same product has different names depending on where you live. Like how some people say soda and others say pop. I always say soda. But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, yeah, those energetic periods definitely take up the majority of the time lately.

doctor.question: During these past two years, have there been times when your 'heavy' or 'gray' feelings were so severe that you could not function at work or at home, or felt completely unable to experience any pleasure in things you usually enjoy for two weeks or more?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest

patient.answer: Yeah, definitely. There are these long stretches, definitely more than two weeks, where I just can't bring myself to do anything I normally love. Things I used to look forward to, like my book club, or cooking, going to art galleries, even just tending to my rose beds... they all just feel like these massive chores that I keep putting off. The roses especially. I have these beautiful David Austin roses, the 'Gertrude Jekyll' variety. They're supposed to have this incredible, strong old rose scent, but you have to prune them just right or they get all leggy. I bought these special pruning shears from a catalog last spring. The catalog was from this company in England, and everything in it looked so perfectly manicured. They had these gorgeous copper watering cans, too. I almost bought one, but my husband said it was ridiculous to spend that much on a watering can when the plastic one from the hardware store works just fine. He's always so practical like that. Sometimes I wish he'd just let me have something pretty just for the sake of it, you know? But anyway, yeah, when I get in those gray moods, I don't even care about the roses or the book club or anything. It's just too much effort.

doctor.question: During these past two years and five months, have these periods of feeling 'up' and feeling 'down' occurred for at least half of the time?

target_item.manifestation: Looking back, the expansive, overcommitted periods have taken up more of the past couple of years than the depressed stretches or the calmer gaps in between.

patient.answer: Yeah, I'd say so. Looking back, those periods where I'm just so... expansive, you know, overcommitted and doing everything, they've actually taken up more of the past couple of years than the depressed stretches or the calmer gaps in between. It's like I'm always on the go. Which reminds me, I signed up to organize the neighborhood block party this year. It's a huge undertaking, really. We're going to have a bouncy house for the kids and a potluck. I've been trying to find a good recipe for a pasta salad that doesn't use mayonnaise, because mayo goes bad so quickly in the sun. My aunt Clara used to make this amazing macaroni salad with celery and little cubes of cheddar cheese, but she always used Miracle Whip. I don't really like the sweetness of Miracle Whip. It tastes too artificial to me. I prefer real mayonnaise if I'm going to use it, like Hellmann's. Or Best Foods, I think they call it out West. It's funny how the same product has different names depending on where you live. Like how some people say soda and others say pop. I always say soda. But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, yeah, those energetic periods definitely take up the majority of the time lately.
